newsitem.title: UK: UK grains OK after cold, but low moisture worrying.
newsitem.headline: UK grains OK after cold, but low moisture worrying.

text.p: The UK grain crop shook off the cold weather that started this year without too much trouble, but now analysts are starting to worry about a lack of moisture.
There's been "not much, if any, loss as a result of the cold," one said.
He could identify some problems in eastern areas, hit by cold winds without snow cover to protect crops and expressed concern over barley in some northern areas. But any problem was minimal, he said.
The UK crop had a good start due to record autumn soil nitrogen levels, which put it in a good position to come out of the cold snap well.
Record high nitrogen is largely a result of low rainfall, which meant less leeching out of the soil, as well as of warm soil temperatures, which encouraged nitrogen crystallisation.
Even though the UK crop looks good now, "if it continues dry it could run out of steam," the analyst said. "Let's have some rain in February and March and we could have a good year."
